[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-017-extension-design-system-integration-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Customer extensions need to integrate with Gainwell's design system for UI consistency. Without standardized integration patterns, many extensions build custom components that diverge from design standards, creating inconsistent user experiences, accessibility violations, and duplicate development costs across states.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-017-extension-design-system-integration-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Standardize how customer extensions consume design system components through npm package imports per IP classification (PTN-GOV-CUS-004), ThemeProvider integration for consistent theming, component composition patterns instead of custom development, and design token usage for styling. Drives high design system adoption, improved customer satisfaction, and reduced accessibility violations.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-017-extension-design-system-integration-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

Apply this pattern when:
- Customer extensions require UI components (PTN-APP-EXT-012 React components)
- Building React component extensions per PTN-GOV-CUS-003 UI decision
- Ensuring visual consistency between extensions and host application
- Implementing accessible UI components in extensions (WCAG 2.2 AA)
- Migrating from ASP.NET server controls to React (522 legacy apps)
- State-specific UI workflows requiring custom interfaces
page_texts.7:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-017-extension-design-system-integration-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- **UI Consistency**: Extensions match host application look/feel; users can't distinguish extension from native UI
- **Accelerated Development**: Pre-built components reduce development time significantly compared to building custom components
- **Accessibility Built-in**: Design system components meet WCAG 2.2 AA standards; automated testing; 0 violations
- **Theme Support**: Extensions inherit application theming automatically (light/dark mode, tenant branding)
- **Cost Savings**: Avoided duplicate development through component reuse across state implementations
- **Maintainability**: Design system updates propagate to all extensions; centralized bug fixes

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-017-extension-design-system-integration-pattern.md#target-audience]

## Target Audience

This pattern is intended for:

- **.NET Developer**: Consumes design system components, ThemeProvider, and design tokens when building React extension UI.
- **Application Architect**: Defines design system adoption requirements and enforces component reuse policies during extension architecture review.
- **DDI Engineer**: Builds state-specific UI extensions using design system components for consistency and accessibility compliance.
- **Platform Engineer**: Maintains design system npm packages, Azure Artifacts registry, and version update processes.
page_texts.10:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-017-extension-design-system-integration-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

**Design System Investment**: Gainwell built a comprehensive design system with 150+ React components (Button, DataGrid, Card, Form inputs, Charts) to enable component reuse across state implementations.

**Design System Adoption Gap**: A significant portion of UI extensions build custom components that duplicate design system functionality. Extensions using design system components consistently achieve higher customer satisfaction than those using custom-styled components.

**Duplicate Development**: Analysis found multiple states independently building similar chart and form validation components that could have reused design system equivalents. This represents substantial avoidable development cost.

**Inconsistent User Experience**: Extensions with custom components don't match host application styling, confusing users and increasing support ticket volume for pages with custom-styled extensions.

**Accessibility Impact**: WCAG 2.2 AA violations occur in extensions with custom components, not in those using design system components. Section 508 audit failures require costly remediation. Design system components have built-in accessibility support.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-017-extension-design-system-integration-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

**Design System Architecture**: @gainwell/design-system-react npm package contains 150+ components built with React 18, TypeScript, styled-components. Three-tier access model per PTN-GOV-CUS-004: Public (80 components), Partner (50 components), Internal (20 components). Published to Azure Artifacts npm registry.

**12 React-Ready Products**: ClaimsPro, MMIS Portal, ProviderConnect, and 9 others migrated to React 18; use design system as foundation. Extensions must use design system to maintain consistency.

**ThemeProvider Pattern**: Design system uses styled-components ThemeProvider for consistent theming. Extensions wrap root component in ThemeProvider to inherit theme tokens (colors, typography, spacing). Supports light/dark mode and tenant branding (PTN-APP-MTN-013).

**Design Tokens**: Design system exports 240+ design tokens (colors, spacing, typography, borders, shadows) as JavaScript objects and CSS variables. Extensions use tokens for custom styling to maintain consistency even when composing custom layouts.

**npm Package Tiers**: Three scoped packages for IP management: @gainwell/design-system-react (full, 420KB), @gainwell/design-system-react-public (Tier 1, 180KB), @gainwell/design-system-react-partner (Tiers 1+2, 320KB). Extensions install package matching IP classification.
page_texts.12:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-017-extension-design-system-integration-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

**Problem 1: Extensions Building Custom Components Duplicating Design System**
_Symptom_: Texas builds custom Button component with state-specific styling instead of using design system Button.
_Root Cause_: Developers unfamiliar with design system catalog; easier to build custom than learn design system; no enforcement.
_Impact_: Significantly longer development time compared to using design system components; inconsistent styling; accessibility issues.

**Problem 2: Inconsistent Styling Due to Missing ThemeProvider**
_Symptom_: California extension uses design system components but colors don't match host app; light theme in extension, dark theme in host.
_Root Cause_: Extension doesn't wrap root in ThemeProvider; components use default theme instead of inheriting host theme.
_Impact_: Visual disconnect confuses users; support tickets; 3-day hotfix to add ThemeProvider.

**Problem 3: Style Overrides Breaking Design System Consistency**
_Symptom_: Florida extension overrides design system Button component CSS; custom colors, font sizing, padding.
_Root Cause_: State wants branded colors; doesn't understand tenant theming (PTN-APP-MTN-013); hacks CSS.
_Impact_: Breaks responsive design; accessibility contrast violations; maintenance burden when design system updates.

**Problem 4: Hardcoded Colors/Spacing Instead of Design Tokens**
_Symptom_: Illinois extension uses `color: #3366cc` and `padding: 16px` instead of design tokens.
_Root Cause_: Developers don't know tokens exist; faster to hardcode during development.
_Impact_: Doesn't adapt to theme changes; breaks dark mode; inconsistent with design system spacing scale.

**Problem 5: Accessibility Violations in Custom Components**
_Symptom_: Ohio extension custom dropdown not keyboard accessible; missing ARIA labels.
_Root Cause_: Built custom dropdown instead of design system Select component with built-in accessibility.
_Impact_: Section 508 audit failure; extended remediation period; significant cost; legal risk.

**Problem 6: Design System Version Mismatches**
_Symptom_: Texas extension uses v1.8 of design system; host app upgraded to v2.3; breaking changes in Button API.
_Root Cause_: Extension npm package.json locks old version; no process for synchronized upgrades.
_Impact_: Runtime errors; Button doesn't render; emergency patch required.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-017-extension-design-system-integration-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

**Competing Forces:**
- **Consistency vs Flexibility**: Extensions need design system consistency, but states want custom branding
- **Reuse vs Development Speed**: Learning design system catalog takes time upfront; faster to build custom short-term
- **Design System Evolution vs Stability**: Design system adds features; breaking changes impact extensions
- **IP Protection vs Access**: PTN-GOV-CUS-004 restricts Partner/Internal tier access; limits component availability

**Hard Constraints:**
- **Design System Mandatory**: PTN-GOV-CUS-004 requires design system usage; custom components prohibited (exceptions rare)
- **IP Classification Access**: State-Exclusive extensions limited to Public tier (80 components); Gainwell-Owned access full catalog
- **WCAG 2.2 AA**: All UI components must meet accessibility standards; design system provides compliance
- **React 18+**: Design system requires React 18 for concurrent features; extensions must match
- **ThemeProvider Required**: Extensions must wrap in ThemeProvider for theme inheritance; architecture review enforces
- **No Style Overrides**: Overriding design system component CSS prohibited; use composition instead
- **Version Alignment**: Extension design system version must align with host app (±1 minor version)
page_texts.15:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-017-extension-design-system-integration-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

**Standardized Design System Integration** defines how extensions consume design system components through npm package installation per IP classification, ThemeProvider wrapping for theme inheritance, component composition patterns for layouts, and design token usage for custom styling. Extensions must use design system components instead of building custom; architecture review enforces compliance.

**Key Principles:**
1. **Design System First**: Use design system components for all UI; custom components prohibited unless design system lacks functionality
2. **Theme Inheritance**: Wrap extension root in ThemeProvider; inherit host app theme (colors, typography, spacing)
3. **Composition Over Customization**: Compose design system components for complex layouts; avoid overriding styles
4. **Design Tokens for Custom Styles**: Use exported design tokens (colors, spacing, typography) for custom styling; no hardcoded values
5. **IP-Based Package Access**: Install npm package matching IP classification (Public/Partner/Internal per PTN-GOV-CUS-004)
6. **Version Alignment**: Keep design system package version within ±1 minor version of host app; coordinate upgrades
7. **Accessibility by Default**: Design system components ensure WCAG 2.2 AA compliance; extensions inherit compliance

page_texts.18:
[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-017-extension-design-system-integration-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

**Installation Flow:**
1. Extension team requests design system access (Architecture Review)
2. IP classification determined per PTN-GOV-CUS-002 (Gainwell-Owned, State-Exclusive, Customer-Owned, Shared)
3. PTN-GOV-CUS-004 maps IP class to design system tier (State-Exclusive → Public, Gainwell-Owned → Full)
4. npm token provisioned with tier access (Azure AD service principal)
5. Extension configures .npmrc with registry and token
6. npm install @gainwell/design-system-react-{tier}

**Theme Inheritance Flow:**
1. Host application renders with DesignSystemThemeProvider at root
2. Host ThemeProvider sets theme object (colors, typography, spacing, dark mode flag)
3. Extension loaded at extension point; extension root wraps in ThemeProvider
4. Extension ThemeProvider inherits theme from host via React Context
5. Extension components receive theme via styled-components props.theme
6. Tenant-specific branding (PTN-APP-MTN-013) overrides theme tokens dynamically

**Component Usage Flow:**
1. Extension imports design system components (Button, Card, Input, DataGrid)
2. Extension composes components into layouts (Card with Form inputs and Button)
3. For custom styling, extension imports design tokens (tokens.colors.primary, tokens.spacing.medium)
4. Extension uses styled-components with design tokens for custom containers/layouts
5. Design system components render with theme-aware styling
6. Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) ensured by design system component implementation

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-017-extension-design-system-integration-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

**Variation 1: Public Tier Only (State-Exclusive Extensions)**
State-Exclusive IP classification (per PTN-GOV-CUS-004) limited to Public tier (80 components: Button, Input, Card, DataTable, Alert, Badge, etc.). Suitable for 80% of extension use cases. Lowest bundle size (~180KB). No advanced components (AdvancedDataGrid, Charts, AdminPanel).

**Variation 2: Partner Tier (Gainwell-Owned Higher-Value Extensions)**
Gainwell-Owned extensions access Partner tier (+50 components: AdvancedDataGrid, Charts, KanbanBoard, RichTextEditor). Enables complex data visualizations and workflows. Bundle size ~320KB. Requires partner-tier npm package.

**Variation 3: Full Catalog (Internal Tools)**
Internal Gainwell tools access all 150 components (Public + Partner + Internal 20 components: AdminPanel, DebugConsole, Telemetry Widgets). Not available to customer extensions. Bundle size ~420KB.

**Variation 4: Custom Theming for Tenant Branding (PTN-APP-MTN-013)**
Extensions supporting tenant-specific branding integrate with Tenant Theme Registry. ThemeProvider receives tenant-specific color overrides, logo URL, custom fonts. Design system components adapt to tenant theme. Adds ~15KB bundle size for theme logic.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-017-extension-design-system-integration-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

1. **Always Use Design System Components**: 150+ components cover 95% of UI needs; building custom duplicates effort and breaks consistency
2. **Wrap Extension Root with ThemeProvider**: Mandatory for theme inheritance; ensures extension matches host app styling (light/dark mode, tenant branding)
3. **Use Design Tokens for Custom Styling**: Import tokens object; use tokens.colors.primary, tokens.spacing.medium instead of hardcoded values; maintains consistency
4. **Follow Component Composition Patterns**: Compose Card + Button + Badge for complex UIs; don't build custom equivalents
5. **Keep Design System Version Aligned**: Extension version within ±1 minor version of host app; coordinate upgrades; check package-lock.json
6. **Reference Storybook Documentation**: Design system Storybook shows component props, examples, accessibility notes; primary reference
7. **Avoid Overriding Component Styles**: Don't use CSS overrides on design system components; breaks responsive design and accessibility; use composition instead
8. **Test with Multiple Themes**: Verify extension works in light mode, dark mode, tenant-specific themes; use themed snapshot tests
9. **Validate Accessibility**: axe-core automated tests + manual keyboard/screen reader testing; design system provides baseline compliance
10. **Use TypeScript for Component Props**: Design system exports TypeScript definitions; enables autocomplete, compile-time errors, refactoring

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-017-extension-design-system-integration-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

**Pitfall 1: Building Custom Components Duplicating Design System Functionality**
**Symptom**: Texas extension builds custom Button component with loading indicator; design system Button has built-in loading prop.
**Why**: Developer unfamiliar with design system catalog; didn't check Storybook documentation.
**How to Avoid**: Search Storybook before building custom; 95% of needs covered; architecture review enforces.
**Example**: Texas spent 3 days building CustomLoadingButton; design system Button has `loading={true}` prop built-in; wasted effort.

**Pitfall 2: Missing ThemeProvider Wrapper Causing Styling Issues**
**Symptom**: California extension Button colors don't match host app; host is dark mode, extension shows light mode colors.
**Why**: Extension forgot to wrap root in ThemeProvider; components use default theme instead of inheriting host theme.
**How to Avoid**: Mandatory ThemeProvider wrapper at extension entry point; architecture review checklist item.
**Example**: California extension visual disconnect caused user confusion; hotfix added ThemeProvider; resolved.

**Pitfall 3: Overriding Design System Component Styles Breaking Consistency**
**Symptom**: Florida extension overrides Button CSS with state-branded blue (#0047AB); conflicts with tenant theme system; breaks responsive and hover states.
**Why**: State wanted custom branding; didn't use tenant theming pattern (PTN-APP-MTN-013); hacked CSS overrides.
**How to Avoid**: Tenant branding via ThemeProvider token overrides; never CSS overrides on design system components.
**Example**: Florida Button override broke responsive design on mobile; hover state incorrect; removed override, used tenant theme tokens.

**Pitfall 4: Hardcoded Colors/Spacing Instead of Design Tokens**
**Symptom**: Illinois extension uses `padding: 16px` and `color: #3366cc` for custom container; doesn't adapt to theme changes; breaks dark mode.
**Why**: Faster to hardcode during development; developer didn't know tokens exist.
**How to Avoid**: Import `tokens` from design system; use `tokens.spacing.medium` and `tokens.colors.primary`.
**Example**: Illinois hardcoded #3366cc blue; dark mode changed primary to #66a3ff; Illinois extension still showed old blue; inconsistent.

**Pitfall 5: Design System Version Mismatch with Host Application**
**Symptom**: Texas extension uses design system v1.8; host app upgraded to v2.3; Button API changed (`onClick` renamed to `onPress`); extension breaks.
**Why**: Extension package.json locked v1.8; no process for synchronized upgrades; breaking change deployed.
**How to Avoid**: CI/CD check enforces version within ±1 minor; coordinate major upgrades with host app releases; test in staging.
**Example**: Texas Button runtime error "onClick is not a function"; emergency patch to v2.3; 4-hour outage.

[patterns/application/extensions/PTN-APP-EXT-017-extension-design-system-integration-pattern.md#compliance-requirements]

### Compliance Requirements

**Design System Mandatory**: PTN-GOV-CUS-004 requires extensions use design system components; custom components prohibited (rare exceptions require ARB approval). Architecture review enforces.

**IP-Based Access**: State-Exclusive → Public tier (80 components), Gainwell-Owned → Partner tier (+50), Internal tools → Full (+20).
**Theme Inheritance**: ThemeProvider wrapper mandatory; extensions must inherit host theme.
**Accessibility**: WCAG 2.2 AA required; design system provides baseline; automated axe-core + manual testing.
**Version Alignment**: Design system version within ±1 minor of host app; prevents breaking changes.
**No Style Overrides**: Overriding design system component CSS prohibited; use composition or tenant theming.

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Customer extensions need to integrate with Gainwell's design system, but without standardized patterns, extensions build custom components creating inconsistent user experiences.

**Solution:** Standardize design system integration through npm package imports, theme provider integration, component composition patterns, and design token usage.

**When to Use:** Customer extensions requiring UI components, building React component extensions, ensuring visual consistency, or implementing accessible UI.

**Key Benefits:**
- UI consistency with host application
- Accelerated development with pre-built components
- Built-in accessibility compliance

**Implementation Complexity:** Low-Medium

**Prerequisites:** @gainwell/design-system-react npm package access, React 18+, styled-components/emotion, npm registry authentication

**Related Patterns:** PTN-GOV-CUS-004 (Design System IP), PTN-APP-EXT-012 (React Components), PTN-APP-MTN-013 (Tenant Theming)
